reasons: The candidate uses a fixed range [5m]; the converter may only use [$__rate_interval], so the PromQL is not what the converter should produce.

The Datadog filters $db (prefix db) and $host (prefix host) are dropped. The expected matchers are postgresql_database_name=~"$db" and host_name=~"$host" (host_name is observed in the dataset). Without them the candidate covers a different set of series.
The $scope variable has no prefix and default *, so dropping it is correct. The $table variable is not used by the query, so it does not apply.

postgresql.tup_inserted is the same quantity as Datadog postgresql.rows_inserted (rows inserted per database), so the metric mapping is acceptable. rate() on the monotonic sum is valid, and avg by postgresql_database_name matches the grouping, which is an observed label.
An exact translation exists, so translated is the right outcome; the defect is in the PromQL itself.
